title: ACP: PromptResponse usage omits cached/thought tokens, inflating client cost estimates

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a detailed, actionable report with clear reproduction context and pinpoints the specific file packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.ts where cached and thought tokens are omitted from ACP usage reporting.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The fix is localized to packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.ts to capture cachedContentTokenCount and thoughtsTokenCount from usageMetadata and populate standard usage fields in the ACP PromptResponse object, alongside corresponding unit test additions in acpSession.test.ts.

summary.problem: When running as an ACP server, token usage reporting omits cached and thought token counts from Gemini usageMetadata.
summary.root_cause: In packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.ts, the GeminiEventType.Finished handler only reads promptTokenCount and candidatesTokenCount from usageMetadata, ignoring cachedContentTokenCount and thoughtsTokenCount.
summary.context: ACP clients estimating costs treat all input tokens as uncached when cachedReadTokens is omitted or zero, significantly overestimating costs during long agentic sessions.

steps: In packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.ts, extract cachedContentTokenCount and thoughtsTokenCount from usageMetadata in the GeminiEventType.Finished event handler.
Accumulate total cached and thought tokens across session turns in prompt().
Populate standard PromptResponse usage fields including inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedReadTokens, thoughtTokens, and totalTokens in prompt().

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: PromptResponse returned by Session.prompt includes cachedReadTokens and thoughtTokens matching the usageMetadata provided in Gemini stream events.
verification_steps: Add unit tests in packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.test.ts with usageMetadata containing promptTokenCount, candidatesTokenCount, cachedContentTokenCount, and thoughtsTokenCount.
Assert that prompt() returns usage metadata containing accurate inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedReadTokens, and thoughtTokens.
